finding.claim: deleteAccount ignores the boolean result of canDelete, so any caller can delete any account (broken authorization / IDOR).
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) entry point; id comes from the URL
account loaded by request id with no owner check
canDelete returns a boolean, but the result is discarded; nothing is thrown or returned

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (line 9) is correct but its result is not enforced. The sibling closeAccount uses assertCanDelete, which throws, so the intended guard exists but was not used here. No other middleware is present in the repo. A nonexistent id gives a null account, which would NPE inside canDelete, but that does not stop deletion of existing accounts.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (AccountService.java:9) returns a boolean, but the call at line 22 discards it. assertCanDelete (line 13) throws on failure but is only used in closeAccount (line 29). No other middleware or callers exist in the repo.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the bare statement `canDelete(u, a);` discards its boolean result, so `accounts.remove(id)` at line 23 runs for any authenticated user on any existing account, unlike closeAccount, which calls the throwing assertCanDelete at line 29.
